For convention and event centers, this data is essential for planning future infrastructure investments and justifying space rental fees. The same room-utilization analytics applies to any physical space that manages bookable rooms and shared areas.

### How does restaurant and buffet analytics work?

Flame measures guest flow in hotel dining areas: breakfast buffet footfall by time slot, restaurant occupancy, average dwell time, and seasonal demand patterns. This data enables optimizing food preparation (reducing food waste by adjusting quantities to forecast traffic), planning waiter shifts based on real demand, and managing peak-hour queues with proactive guest information. A hotel that knows 65% of guests have breakfast between 8:00 and 9:30 can stagger resources accordingly. Documented food-waste reduction in hotels with footfall analytics is 10-20%, with the added benefit of improving guest experience by reducing wait times. The same flow analytics applies to dining areas in shopping malls, retail spaces, and other physical spaces.

### Can it optimize check-in and the lobby?

Yes. Flame measures lobby traffic patterns and check-in queues, providing data to optimize the arrival experience. Key metrics: lobby footfall by hour, reception wait times, traffic distribution between staffed check-in and automated kiosks. This data enables aligning reception staffing with arrival peaks, evaluating self-service kiosk effectiveness, and designing lobby flow to reduce congestion. Hotels also use lobby analytics to measure non-residential traffic (restaurant visitors, event attendees) and optimize security and services accordingly. All without identifying any individual guest, using only anonymous counting and flow analysis. Similar queue and flow optimization applies in retail stores, shopping malls, and other physical spaces.

### What metrics does it provide that the PMS doesn't?

The PMS (Property Management System) measures room occupancy, revenue, and bookings, but is blind to physical guest behavior outside the room. Flame complements the PMS with metrics that hotel management systems don't capture: real use of common areas (pool, gym, spa), movement patterns between spaces, wait times at reception and restaurant, attendance at hotel events, and real meeting room utilization rate (vs. booked). API integration between Flame and the PMS enables correlating this data: do premium-package guests use the spa more? Do long-stay guests frequent the restaurant more? These correlations guide package creation, service pricing, and facility investment allocation. The same principle of complementing existing management systems applies to Flame integrations in retail stores, shopping malls, and other physical spaces.

### How is guest privacy guaranteed?

Guest privacy is paramount in hospitality. Flame guarantees total anonymity: the system counts silhouettes and analyzes flows without identifying, tracking, or profiling any individual guest. No facial recognition, no video storage, no biometric data collection. The data generated is exclusively statistical: 42 people used the spa between 14:00 and 16:00, average reception wait time was 3.2 minutes. It is impossible to link this data to a specific guest. The cameras used are those of the existing security circuit, already covered by video surveillance legislation. Flame adds an analytical layer that produces only aggregated data. Verified GDPR compliance, EU processing, ISO 27001 certification. The same privacy-by-design architecture protects visitors across all Flame deployments, from retail stores and shopping malls to any other physical space.

### How does analytics improve museum management?

Foot traffic analytics in cultural and public spaces measures real visitor behavior: preferred routes, rooms with the longest dwell time, congestion zones, and signage effectiveness. A reference cultural institution uses Flame to optimize exhibition flow, ensuring visitors complete the entire route. Data revealed that 40% of visitors didn't reach the last rooms, leading to a signage redesign that increased average visit duration from 42 to 58 minutes. For physical spaces with time-slot entry, room occupancy analytics prevents saturation and improves the experience. Footfall metrics are also essential for justifying public funding and reporting on exhibition impact.

### What solutions exist for public transportation?

Flame provides footfall analytics for public transportation physical spaces, measuring passenger flow, wait times at access controls, and zone occupancy. Data enables optimizing service frequency based on real demand, planning security and cleaning staffing, and improving signage to distribute passenger flow. All processing is completely anonymous: Flame counts silhouettes without identifying any passenger. Integrations with management systems enable automatic occupancy-based actions, such as activating additional turnstiles or modifying information panel messages. Hypersensor's scalability enables covering complex physical spaces with dozens of access points using the existing camera infrastructure.

### How does it help in sports and entertainment venues?

Flame's analytics in sports and entertainment physical spaces measures access flows, occupancy by grandstand zone, traffic in food service and merchandising areas, and evacuation times. This data enables optimizing the attendee experience: reducing access queues by opening additional doors based on demand, sizing food service points based on zone traffic, and planning evacuation with real flow data. For venue managers, analytics provides per-event performance metrics: how early do attendees arrive? Which food service zones are saturated? How long does exit take? All without any individual identification, only anonymous counts and flows processed through existing security cameras.

### Can it help with urban planning?

Yes. Flame provides foot traffic data for urban physical spaces that informs urban planning decisions. Metrics include: pedestrian traffic patterns by hour and day, flow maps showing preferred routes, concentration zones, and traffic distribution across different access points. This data replaces ad hoc surveys (expensive, infrequent, imprecise) with continuous and objective measurement. City councils use this information to decide where to install urban furniture, how to design pedestrianization of streets, and evaluate the impact of urban changes on pedestrian flow. All processing is anonymous and GDPR-compliant, generating only aggregated statistical data.

### How does occupancy management work at large events?

Flame provides real-time crowd management for large events, festivals, and mass gatherings. The system monitors entries and exits, calculates current occupancy and projects it based on arrival trends, allowing peaks to be anticipated before they occur. Configurable threshold alerts (70%, 85%, 95% of capacity) are sent automatically to security and organization teams. For festivals with multiple stages, Flame measures occupancy by zone, allowing the public to be redirected to less crowded areas through digital signage or PA announcements. Historical data from previous events enables improving planning for each edition. All processing is anonymous: Flame counts silhouettes without identifying attendees.

### What benefits does it bring to libraries and educational centers?

Educational physical spaces use Flame's analytics to optimize schedules, spaces, and resources. Key metrics: footfall by hour and day of the week (to adjust opening hours), study room occupancy (to implement reservation systems based on real use), traffic by zone (to decide which collections need more space), and seasonal patterns (to plan resources during exam periods). Analytics demonstrate real facility use with objective data, which is fundamental for justifying budgets and applying for funding. An educational center showing 2,000 daily visitors with peaks of 400 simultaneous users during exams has a powerful tool to request space expansion or extended hours. All with total privacy: only anonymous counts.

### What is a People Counting system and how does it work?

A People Counting system, or software, uses physical sensors (typically video cameras or infrared beams) to record how many people enter and exit a physical space. Modern software like Flame Analytics applies AI video analytics to existing cameras, eliminating the need for dedicated hardware. Flame's Hypersensor technology processes video streams in real time, detecting and counting people through silhouette recognition without identifying faces or using biometric data. Flame reaches over 99% accuracy in physical spaces, stores, and shopping malls across 7 countries. Unlike traditional infrared counters that only measure door crossings, AI video counting works across complete zones, distinguishing employees from visitors.

### How accurate is AI People Counting compared to manual counting?

AI-based People Counting like Flame's reaches over 99% accuracy in controlled environments, far surpassing manual counting, which typically delivers 75-85% accuracy due to human fatigue and distraction. Flame's Hypersensor uses deep learning models trained on millions of real-world scenarios to maintain accuracy even in high-density environments such as shopping mall corridors or store entrances during peak hours. The system self-calibrates using historical patterns and handles complex scenarios (groups walking together, people with large bags, wheelchair users) that cause traditional infrared or thermal sensors to undercount by 15-30%. Accuracy is validated through field audits for enterprise clients, including leading retailers, shopping mall operators, and organizations managing physical spaces.

### How much does a People Counting system for a store cost?

Total cost depends on three factors: number of entrances to monitor, existing camera infrastructure, and analytics modules selected. Flame can work with the client's existing cameras, though it will depend on camera quality and proper placement and calibration, eliminating the per-entrance cost of dedicated sensors. Software licenses follow a SaaS model with monthly or annual subscriptions. For a single location with 2-4 cameras, expect EUR 150-400/month, including People Counting, basic traffic analytics, and dashboard access. Organizations with multiple locations—from a large fuel retailer (over 1,000 stations) to a network of physical spaces—benefit from volume pricing. ROI typically materializes in 3-6 months through staffing optimization alone, reducing labor costs by 8-15%.

### What is the ROI of implementing People Counting?

Organizations using Flame's People Counting—whether they manage physical spaces, stores, or shopping malls—achieve measurable ROI in 90 days across three areas. First, conversion rate visibility: knowing the real ratio of visitors who buy reveals whether low sales are due to lack of traffic or poor in-store experience. Second, staffing optimization: aligning employee shifts with real traffic patterns reduces labor costs by 8-15% and improves visitor service during peak hours. Third, marketing attribution: measuring footfall lift after campaigns demonstrates which promotions truly generate visits. Flame clients from the portfolio of leading sector operators with 10 shopping malls increased their tenants' conversion rates by an average of 12% in the first year.

### Is People Counting GDPR-compliant?

Yes, when implemented correctly. Flame's People Counting is privacy by design: the system counts anonymous silhouettes moving through the space without capturing, storing, or processing biometric data. No facial recognition, no individual tracking, no personal data collection. Data is aggregated into statistical counts—147 visitors between 10:00 and 11:00—making it impossible to identify any individual. Flame holds ISO 27001 certification and processes all data on EU servers. The system generates only aggregated metrics (hourly counts, occupancy levels by zone, average dwell times), never individual profiles. This approach exceeds GDPR requirements and applies equally to physical spaces, stores, and shopping malls.

### Does it work with my existing video surveillance cameras?

Yes, and this is Flame's key differentiator. Flame's Hypersensor technology connects to existing IP cameras via RTSP protocol, transforming video surveillance infrastructure into business intelligence with no new hardware. Compatible with major camera brands including Axis, Hikvision, Dahua, Bosch, and Hanwha. Requirements are minimal: cameras need at least 720p resolution and a top-down or angled-from-above mounting position. Flame's technical team performs a free camera audit to confirm compatibility before deployment. In a large fuel retailer's deployment across more than 1,000 service stations, Flame connected to the existing camera network without any hardware purchases, reducing deployment cost by 60%. The same approach applies to physical spaces, stores, and shopping malls.

### What's the difference between real-time and historical data?

Real-time data shows current occupancy and traffic flow as it happens, essential for immediate decisions like opening additional service points or activating capacity management protocols in physical spaces. Historical data reveals patterns across weeks, months, and years, enabling strategic decisions about opening hours, seasonal staffing, and layout changes. Flame provides both through a unified dashboard. Real-time data refreshes every 15 seconds with configurable threshold alerts. Historical analytics includes year-over-year comparisons, day-of-week patterns, and weather correlation analysis. Physical spaces use real-time data for operations, while shopping malls and stores rely on historical data for quarterly business reviews and lease negotiations.

The process: Days 1-2, camera audit and RTSP connection setup (remote); Days 3-4, AI model calibration for your specific environment; Days 5-7, dashboard configuration and team training. No on-site hardware installation is required when using existing cameras. ### How is the conversion rate calculated?

Flame divides POS tickets by unique visitors counted by the cameras within a time window. Segmentable by hour, day, zone, category or salesperson.

### Does it work with any POS?

Yes. Native connectors for major systems (Toshiba, NCR, ICG, Cegid, Mistral) plus open API and scheduled CSV imports for custom setups.

### How long until we see data?

Traffic data is available 5–7 days after signing. POS integration usually adds 1–2 weeks depending on the system. Full conversion live within 30 days.

### Can we measure conversion by product category?

Yes, if your POS sends the category with each ticket. Flame correlates zone traffic (cameras) with category sales (POS) to reveal which products convert in which areas.

### Is it GDPR compliant?

Yes. Flame counts anonymous silhouettes, never personal data. POS data is crossed at aggregate time-window level, never per individual.

Most retailers see 3–8% lift in conversion and 8–15% lower labor cost through smarter staffing. Payback typically under 12 months.

### How is queue length detected?

Through AI video analysis on existing CCTV. Flame measures queue size, occupancy of waiting areas and average wait time without needing physical sensors.

Above 95% accuracy in standard service environments. The model accounts for group behavior and varied queue shapes.

### What is foot traffic analytics and why does it matter in retail?

Foot traffic analytics is the systematic measurement and analysis of footfall in physical spaces: how many people visit, when they come, how long they stay, and which areas they frequent. For any space manager, it answers the fundamental question: is my problem traffic or conversion? A store with 500 daily visitors and 50 sales has a 10% conversion rate, meaning marketing should focus on the in-store experience, not on attracting more traffic. The same logic applies to any physical space with a retail area. Flame's Traffic Insights module processes data from existing cameras and people counters to deliver footfall metrics broken down by hour, day, zone, and entrance. Clients like leading real estate consultancies use this data to benchmark properties against their portfolio averages.

### What is zone counting and how can it improve my store layout?

Zones analytics divides your physical space into defined areas and measures traffic, dwell time, and transition patterns for each zone independently. Flame uses existing overhead cameras to create invisible boundary lines without physical sensors or beacons. The result is a clear picture of which zones attract attention, which are dead spots, and how visitors flow between areas. A shopping mall might discover that 40% of visitors never reach the upper floor despite having anchor stores there. Flame's Zones analytics would quantify that lost opportunity and measure the impact of layout changes. Organizations managing physical spaces use Zones analytics to optimize visitor routes, while stores apply it to maximize product exposure.

### How can footfall data optimize staffing?

Staffing optimization is one of the fastest-ROI applications of traffic analytics. Flame's Traffic Insights shows exact hourly traffic patterns for each day of the week, revealing when your space is overstaffed (wasting payroll budget) or understaffed (missing opportunities). The platform generates recommended staffing curves that align employee presence with real visitor traffic. Organizations—from physical spaces managing reception desks to stores optimizing floor coverage—typically find a 20-30% mismatch between staff schedules and traffic peaks. Correcting this reduces labor costs by 8-15% and improves service because visitors receive attention when they need it. Flame clients can export traffic data directly to workforce management systems or use the integrated scheduling recommendations.

### What is conversion analytics in physical retail?

Conversion rate in physical retail is the percentage of store visitors who make a purchase: transactions divided by footfall. It's the most important KPI most retailers can't measure without People Counting technology. A store with 10,000 monthly visitors and 1,500 transactions has a 15% conversion rate. Flame calculates it automatically by integrating footfall data with POS transaction counts. Unlike ecommerce where conversion tracking is standard, physical retail has historically operated blind. Flame closes this gap, enabling stores to set conversion targets, measure promotional impact, and identify which locations have conversion problems versus traffic problems. The same conversion logic extends to shopping mall food courts and stores of all sizes.

### How does weather affect foot traffic and can analytics account for it?

Weather is one of the most influential external factors on physical-space traffic, yet most organizations don't quantify its impact. Flame's Traffic Insights includes weather correlation analysis that overlays local climate data with your footfall patterns. This reveals your location's specific weather sensitivity: some physical spaces lose 30% of traffic on rainy days, while others—like shopping malls—gain 15% as visitors seek indoor alternatives. Understanding this pattern enables better planning: adjusting promotional calendars based on weather forecasts, setting realistic targets that account for conditions, and distinguishing weather-resilient locations from weather-dependent ones across physical spaces, stores, and shopping malls.

### Can I export traffic data to my existing BI tools?

Yes. Flame provides a complete REST API to export all traffic data to your existing business intelligence stack. The most common integrations include Power BI, Tableau, Looker, and Google Data Studio. Data is available via real-time streaming (webhooks) or batch export (CSV, JSON, Excel). API documentation includes pre-built connectors for major BI platforms. Enterprise clients—from leading retailers and shopping mall operators to organizations managing physical spaces—integrate Flame data with their internal analytics platforms to combine footfall with operational, sales, and CRM data in unified reports. Data granularity ranges from 15-minute intervals to annual summaries.

No. Flame uses anonymous silhouette detection and movement tracking.

### What insights can we get?

Heatmaps by floor, top routes, time per zone, interactions between areas, demographic mix and hour-by-hour behavior — all anonymous and aggregate.

### Can we measure the impact of layout changes?

Yes. Compare behavior before and after a layout change to quantify the lift in dwell time, conversion or zone traffic.

### How is data presented?

Through dashboards with heatmaps, flow maps (Sankey), zone interaction matrices and time-series charts. Exportable to BI tools via API.

### How do heatmaps work in retail?

Heatmaps are visual representations of where visitors spend time in your space, shown as color overlays on your floor plan: red for high-traffic and high-dwell zones, blue for low-activity areas. Flame generates heatmaps from existing cameras using AI that tracks the density and duration of anonymous movement without identifying individuals. Key insights include: which displays attract the most attention, where natural gathering points form, which areas get skipped, and how traffic patterns shift between weekdays and weekends. Heatmaps are generated hourly and can be compared across time periods. A leading furniture retailer uses heatmaps to validate the design of its guided store path, while other physical spaces apply them to optimize visitor flow.

### What is dwell time and why does it matter?

Dwell time measures how long visitors spend in a specific zone or across your entire space. It's a critical engagement indicator: longer dwell time in a physical space correlates with higher visitor interaction, while extended dwell time near checkouts or service counters indicates queue problems. Flame measures dwell time anonymously through AI silhouette tracking: no individual is identified, but aggregated statistics reveal the average, median, and time distribution per zone. Physical spaces evaluate visitor engagement (45 seconds in one area versus 3 minutes in another tells a story), shopping malls assess common-area efficiency, and retailers measure display attractiveness.

### How does cross-camera tracking work without biometrics?

The technology works by matching anonymous silhouettes between overlapping camera fields of view. These signatures are temporary, existing only during an individual visit and discarded immediately after. A persistent profile is never created. This approach enables complete visitor journey mapping (visitor entered through North entrance, spent 4 minutes in Zone A, 8 minutes in the store zone, exited through West) while maintaining full GDPR compliance. The system holds ISO 27001 certification and works identically across physical spaces, shopping malls, and stores.

### What is behavioral segmentation in physical spaces?

Behavioral segmentation groups visitors into anonymous categories based on their behavior within the space, without identifying who they are. Flame's analytics distinguishes behavior types: explorers (high dwell time, many zones, no purchase), mission visitors (direct route to one zone, quick interaction), recurring visitors (anonymous repeat-visit patterns detected through traffic analysis). This segmentation is statistical, not individual: Flame tells you that 35% of Saturday-afternoon visitors show explorer behavior, not who those explorers are. Physical spaces use this to understand how visitors interact with different areas, shopping malls optimize tenant placement, and retailers tailor experiences: more staff in explorer-dominated zones, faster service for mission visitors.

### How does Customer Journey optimize store layout?

Customer Journey analytics provides evidence-based guidance for layout decisions, quantifying how visitors actually use your space versus how you intended them to use it. Flame data reveals: which entrance captures the most traffic (crucial for placing key displays or information desks), natural versus forced flow patterns, zone-to-zone transition rates, and dead zones receiving less than 5% of total traffic. A typical optimization cycle: measure baseline flow, identify underperforming zones, make layout changes, measure impact. Flame clients report 15-25% increases in target-zone exposure following data-driven layout changes. A large organization managing a physical space used journey mapping to redesign visitor routes, increasing average visit duration from 42 to 58 minutes.

### Can I measure the impact of promotional displays?

Yes. Flame's A/B testing capability compares visitor behavior before and after display changes, promotions, or layout modifications. Set a measurement period for the before state, make the change, and then measure the after state: Flame automatically controls for day-of-week and time-of-day variations. Compared metrics include: zone traffic lift, dwell time change, flow pattern shifts, and conversion impact. A physical space redesigned its wayfinding signage and measured a 30% reduction in reception dwell time. A large store changed its entrance display from seasonal apparel to electronics and measured a 23% lift in electronics-zone traffic. Promotional impact reports are available within 48 hours of campaign completion.

### How does Customer Journey differ from beacon-based solutions?

Beacon-based solutions require visitors to have a specific app installed with Bluetooth enabled, resulting in opt-in rates typically below 5%, producing statistically biased samples. Flame's camera-based approach captures 100% of visitors automatically, requiring no visitor action. Key differences: beacons need dedicated hardware (EUR 30-50/unit, battery maintenance); Flame uses existing cameras. Beacons provide proximity data (visitor is near a point); Flame delivers complete journeys with zone-to-zone flows. Beacons collect device identifiers (personal data under GDPR); Flame processes only anonymous silhouettes. Whether in a physical space, a store, or a shopping mall, Flame clients get 20x more data through 100% coverage versus beacons' biased 3-5% samples.

You set a usage threshold per restroom. When reached, Flame sends a notification to the cleaning team via the mobile app with priority and location info.

The app is recommended for full traceability. Without it, alerts can be sent via email, SMS or to existing facility management systems via API.

Yes. Each restroom can have its own threshold, schedule and priority. Different rules for peak hours, weekends or events.

### How do automatic occupancy alerts work?

Flame lets you configure multiple alert thresholds for each zone or building. Typical example: yellow alert at 70% capacity (prepare additional resources), orange alert at 85% (activate flow management protocol), red alert at 95% (restrict entries). Alerts are sent by email, SMS, or integrated with building management systems via API. Real-time dashboards display current occupancy with color coding. For physical spaces, alerts trigger visitor flow protocols; for shopping malls, alerts are configured by floor and zone, enabling granular actions (diverting traffic from floor 2 to floor 3) instead of closing the entire mall. Stores use alerts for crowd management during peak hours. Managers can review alert history to identify patterns and plan preventive measures during high-demand periods.

### Does it work with my current cameras?

Yes. Flame connects to existing IP cameras via RTSP protocol to monitor entries and exits. Cameras need to be positioned at access points (entrances/exits) with a top-down or semi-top-down angle for accurate counting. Minimum required resolution: 720p. Compatible with Axis, Hikvision, Dahua, Bosch, Hanwha, and most RTSP-supporting manufacturers. If existing cameras don't cover all access points, Flame performs a technical audit to identify blind spots and recommend the minimum positions needed. In most cases, 80-90% of the necessary cameras are already installed as part of the security system. Typical occupancy deployment—whether for a shopping mall, a store, or any physical space—completes in 5-10 business days.

### How does it improve the visitor experience?

Occupancy management improves visitor experience in three ways. First, proactive information: entrance screens display current occupancy levels and the least crowded areas, allowing visitors to make informed decisions. Second, flow distribution: when a zone reaches high occupancy, digital signage can suggest alternative routes, reducing crowding feel—critical in both physical spaces and shopping malls. Third, service optimization: occupancy levels automatically trigger cleaning protocols, opening of additional service points, and security reinforcement. The result is a more comfortable and better-managed space. Flame-network shopping malls that display occupancy data at entrances report 25% higher comfort perception in visitor satisfaction surveys.

### Which capacity regulations does it help comply with?

Capacity regulations vary by jurisdiction but are universal across European regulatory frameworks. Spain's CTE (Technical Building Code) establishes maximum occupancy densities by use type—applicable to stores, shopping malls, and all types of physical spaces. Regional governments add specific requirements, many derived from COVID-era regulations that have remained in place. Flame provides the necessary tools: real-time occupancy monitoring by zone, historical records for audits, automatic alerts when approaching limits, and exportable compliance reports. For shopping malls and physical spaces, Flame generates capacity compliance certificates that satisfy municipal inspection requirements and insurance audits.

### Does it integrate with building management systems?

Yes. Flame offers API integration with major BMS (Building Management Systems) to automate occupancy-based responses. Typical integrations: HVAC that adjusts ventilation and temperature based on real occupancy, reducing energy consumption by 15-25% across physical spaces, stores, and shopping malls; lighting that activates in occupied zones and dims in empty areas; digital signage that displays occupancy information and alternative routes; and access control systems that restrict entries when thresholds are reached. These integrations transform occupancy management from a monitoring tool into an active building management system. Supported standard protocols include BACnet, Modbus, and REST API.

### What is WiFi marketing and how does it work?

WiFi marketing transforms your guest WiFi network from an operational cost into a visitor acquisition channel. Flame's Connect module provides a customizable login page (captive portal) where visitors register with email, phone, or social media accounts to access WiFi. This creates a consented visitor database tied to visit data: when they come, how often, and how long they stay. Unlike generic guest WiFi, Connect captures first-party data with built-in GDPR compliance. Physical spaces, shopping malls, and stores use this data for segmented email campaigns, proximity promotions, and visit frequency analysis. All data collection requires the visitor's explicit opt-in consent.

### Does it work without changing my WiFi infrastructure?

Yes. Flame's Connect works as a software layer on top of your existing WiFi infrastructure. Compatible with major access-point manufacturers including Cisco Meraki, Aruba, Ruckus, Ubiquiti, and TP-Link. Setup consists of redirecting your guest network's authentication through the Flame Connect platform, a process typically completed in one day. No additional hardware is required. For shopping malls with multiple tenant networks, Flame can create a unified login page that aggregates mall-wide data while each tenant retains visibility into their own visitors. A large fuel retailer deployed Flame across more than 1,000 stations with no additional hardware, reducing deployment costs by 60%. The same approach works for physical spaces of any size.

### How is GDPR compliance handled with WiFi marketing?

Flame's Connect is GDPR-compliant by design. All data collection is consent-based: visitors actively choose to register, select which data to share, and accept the terms of service before accessing WiFi. Commercial communication checkboxes are unchecked by default. Visitors can access WiFi with minimal data (email only) or anonymously if the venue allows it. Data is stored on EU servers with encryption in transit and at rest. GDPR rights (access, rectification, erasure) are managed through the admin panel. Data retention policies are configurable per venue. Connect never collects visitor browsing data or monitors internet activity—only WiFi login and registration data provided voluntarily.

### What data is collected through social login?

Social login lets visitors access WiFi using their Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, or Instagram accounts. The data collected depends on platform permissions and user consent. Typically: name, email address, profile photo, age range, and gender. Everything is received with the visitor's explicit consent and the platform API permissions. Flame's Connect stores these profile data linked to visit data (date, time, location), creating a rich visitor profile for marketing segmentation. Important: social login data is first-party data provided voluntarily, fundamentally different from any form of passive tracking. Typical social login rates: 40-60% choose the social option over email, providing richer profile data with less friction. This applies to physical spaces, shopping malls, and stores alike.

### How can I use WiFi data for segmented campaigns?

Flame's Connect integrates with major email marketing platforms (Mailchimp, HubSpot, Salesforce Marketing Cloud) to trigger campaigns based on visit behavior data. Segments are created automatically: new visitors (welcome message), frequent visitors (loyalty program), inactive visitors (reactivation campaigns), high-dwell-time visitors (highly engaged). Real-world example: a large shopping mall created a "we miss you" campaign targeting visitors who hadn't returned in 30 days, achieving a 12% return rate. Stores apply similar strategies with product-specific campaigns. Campaigns can be triggered automatically by behavior (first visit, fifth visit, 14-day absence) or run manually with filters by location, frequency, and visit time slot.

### Does it integrate with my CRM or email platform?

Yes. Flame's Connect offers native integrations with Mailchimp, HubSpot, Salesforce, ActiveCampaign, and Zoho CRM, plus a REST API to connect with any platform. Visitor data syncs automatically, including email address, visit history, frequency metrics, and engagement scores. For enterprise clients, the API enables bidirectional automations: Flame data enriches CRM profiles with physical visit behavior, while the CRM triggers personalized WiFi messages based on visitor history. A typical integration completes in 2-3 days with the provided API documentation. Flame also supports real-time exports via webhooks for custom marketing automation integrations.

### What is DOOH audience measurement?

It means measuring how many people actually see each digital out-of-home (DOOH) screen, instead of estimating it. In a shopping mall or a store, that means knowing how many people walked past each screen at every time of day, how long they stayed in front of it and how many later visited the advertised store. Brands investing in retail media no longer accept estimates: they want verified audiences. Flame measures it with video analytics on top of your camera network, using aggregated and anonymous data.

### Which retail media metrics does Flame measure for each screen?

The ones premium brands ask for, per campaign, screen and zone: real impressions (how many people were actually in front of each screen at every time of day), customer typology (gender and age band distribution, aggregated and anonymous), dwell time and attention (average time in front of the screen and percentage of effective attention) and drive-to-store (incremental visits to the advertised store amongst exposed vs non-exposed visitors). After every campaign you get a report ready to send to the advertiser, with the key results per screen and zone.

### How do I prove to a brand that its DOOH campaign drove store visits?

With drive-to-store measurement. Flame compares visits to the advertised store between people exposed to the screen and people who were not, isolating the incremental visits generated by the campaign. You can also compare traffic and conversion across pre- and post-campaign periods, by zone or by store. It closes the loop every advertiser asks for: not just how many people saw the ad, but how many walked in afterwards.

### How does it help me sell my screen inventory?

You move from selling screens to selling audiences. With an audited audience, your rate card stops relying on estimates and reflects the real value you deliver. Premium brands ask for real impressions, audience profile and drive-to-store; if your rate card can't deliver them, your inventory competes as filler. With that data per campaign, screen and zone you can justify the price of every screen and prove ROI to brands and agencies.

### Do I need new hardware or a different digital signage CMS?

Usually not. Flame runs on your existing IP camera network: its Hypersensor technology connects to the video streams via RTSP and is compatible with the main brands, such as Axis, Hikvision, Dahua, Bosch and Hanwha, although results depend on camera quality, placement and calibration. It doesn't replace your digital signage CMS or your DOOH platform either: it is an analytics layer independent of the hardware and the CMS that integrates with the systems you already use, and you can export the data via API to BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau or Looker.

### Is it GDPR compliant?

Flame does not use biometric data or identify anyone: it extracts analytical data from the video streams and discards the original images, and no video is stored outside your security system. What you get is aggregated, anonymous data that you can share with your advertisers without exposing any personal information.

### What is guest WiFi marketing for shopping centres?

Guest WiFi marketing for shopping centres turns the free WiFi in the centre into a consented visitor database and a marketing channel. Shoppers sign in through a branded captive portal, choose what they agree to receive, and the centre uses that first-party data for campaigns, events, loyalty and tenant offers. Platforms such as Purple, Aislelabs, Cloud4Wi and Flame Analytics provide the portal, the consent records and the analytics.

### Is WiFi marketing GDPR compliant in Europe?

Yes, when consent is specific, informed and given by a clear affirmative act. Marketing boxes must be unticked by default, purposes must be separated, consent must be recorded and as easy to withdraw as to give, and visitors must be able to have their data erased. Recital 32 of the GDPR states that silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity do not constitute consent. In the UK, PECR also applies to marketing emails.

### What capture rate can a mall captive portal achieve?

According to Flame Analytics, a well designed portal with a clear incentive (free WiFi, a coupon or exclusive content) typically captures 25-40% of connected visitors, and 8-15% without an incentive. Vendors also publish opt-in rates, which use a different denominator: Purple reports an 80% opt-in rate at Highcross Leicester. Compare like with like before benchmarking.

### Does guest WiFi still work with MAC address randomisation?

Yes, but device addresses are no longer a reliable way to recognise returning visitors. iOS 14 and later and Android 11 and later use private, rotating WiFi addresses. Modern platforms recognise returning visitors through the registered login (email or social account), one-line return sign-in or Passpoint profiles instead of the MAC address. Flame Analytics identifies returning visitors through the registered email and behavioural patterns.

### Can WiFi data be combined with footfall counting?

Yes. Some platforms combine WiFi data with counts from third-party sensors (Aislelabs lists people counter integrations such as Xovis). Flame Analytics runs guest WiFi marketing and people counting in the same platform, counting footfall with AI video analytics on the centre's existing CCTV cameras, so the database can be read against real visitor numbers.

### Who owns the visitor data: the mall or the tenants?

The data belongs to whoever the visitor consented to: usually the centre's owner or operator, as the data controller named in the portal. Tenants own the shoppers in their own tills and apps. A centre can share insight with tenants as aggregated figures, or pass contacts to them only with explicit consent for that purpose. Check that the contract states the database belongs to the owner, not the managing agent or the WiFi supplier.

### What are the best alternatives to RetailNext?

The main alternatives are Flame Analytics, V-Count, FootfallCam, ShopperTrak (Sensormatic Solutions) and Xovis. Flame Analytics runs AI video analytics on existing CCTV cameras. V-Count, FootfallCam and Xovis use their own 3D or stereo vision sensors. ShopperTrak is the people counting and analytics line of Sensormatic Solutions. The right choice depends on your cameras, your markets and your privacy requirements.

### Is there a RetailNext alternative that works with existing CCTV cameras?

Yes. Flame Analytics connects to existing IP cameras over RTSP and turns them into people counting, journey and occupancy sensors, with cameras of at least 720p mounted top-down or at an angle. FootfallCam also offers a supermarket package that reuses existing CCTV for queue and aisle analytics. RetailNext's Aurora sensor does not depend on existing cameras, although its Asset Protection video management supports existing analogue or IP cameras.

### Which people counting platforms are GDPR compliant without biometrics?

Flame Analytics, RetailNext, V-Count, FootfallCam and Xovis all describe anonymous counting that does not identify individuals; for ShopperTrak, ask the vendor, as the pages we consulted did not detail it. Flame Analytics counts without biometrics and without storing images. Xovis transmits metadata without biometric or personal information. V-Count and FootfallCam process data on the device. Some vendors offer optional gender and age estimation, so check in your DPIA which features are switched on.

### How do RetailNext and Flame Analytics differ?

RetailNext is a retail-focused platform built on its own Aurora ceiling sensor, which combines counting, behavioural analytics and video, and it is headquartered in California. Flame Analytics is a Spanish platform that applies AI video analytics to the cameras a site already has, covers retail, shopping centres, hospitality and public venues, and processes data without biometrics.

### What should a people counting RFP include?

A pilot in two or three stores, accuracy measured against a manual count at busy and quiet times, a data protection impact assessment, a camera and network audit, the integrations you need (POS, workforce management, BI, SSO), a written deployment plan, a three-year total cost and references in your own country and sector.

### ¿Cuántos KPIs es razonable medir en una tienda?

Entre cuatro y ocho de forma activa. Más de ocho indicadores en un cuadro de mando diario suelen acabar siendo decorativos. Mejor empezar por el cuadro mínimo (afluencia, conversión, ticket medio y colas) y ampliar cuando esos cuatro estén consolidados, integrados y usados por el equipo de tienda.

### ¿Cómo se mide la conversión sin pedir el ticket al cliente?

Cruzando el dato del TPV (número de tickets emitidos) con el dato del sistema de conteo de personas (visitantes que entraron en el mismo periodo). El cálculo es tickets ÷ visitantes × 100. No es necesario identificar al cliente, basta con que ambos sistemas exporten al mismo dashboard con la misma franja horaria.

### ¿Medir estos KPIs es compatible con RGPD?

Sí, siempre que se trabaje con datos agregados y anonimizados. Los sistemas modernos de conteo, heatmap, recorrido y Wi-Fi de invitados están diseñados para no identificar a personas concretas: usan visión por IA que descarta rasgos biométricos, MAC randomizada o consentimiento explícito en el caso de programas de fidelización. La regla práctica es que ningún dato individual debería poder reconstruirse a partir de los KPIs publicados en el cuadro de mando.

### ¿Cuánto cuesta empezar a medir KPIs en retail?

Depende del número de tiendas y de la profundidad de la analítica. Una tienda individual puede activar afluencia, conversión y ticket medio con una inversión modesta en sensor y software. Una cadena de varias tiendas suele requerir una plataforma central que unifique los datos, integrada con TPV y ERP. El criterio sano es empezar pequeño en una tienda piloto, validar que los datos cambian decisiones, y replicar a la red.

### ¿Cómo integro estos KPIs con mi TPV o mi ERP?

La integración estándar se hace por API: el sistema de analítica retail expone endpoints para que el TPV cargue tickets, importes y SKUs, y el ERP consuma los KPIs agregados. Si no hay API, también se puede trabajar con exportaciones programadas (CSV diario) y un ETL ligero. Lo importante es que el flujo sea automático: cualquier paso manual termina por romperse y vacía el cuadro de mando en pocas semanas.

### ¿Qué métricas debería empezar a medir un supermercado?

Las tres mínimas son: tráfico por entrada y por zona, tiempo de permanencia por sección y tiempo medio de espera en cajas. A partir de ahí se puede cruzar con datos de ventas (TPV) y construir un cuadro de mando más rico.

### ¿Cumple la analítica de tráfico con el RGPD?

Sí, siempre que la tecnología empleada no identifique personas. El portal cautivo de Guest WiFi opera con consentimiento expreso del usuario.

### ¿Es rentable para un supermercado pequeño o solo para grandes cadenas?

Hoy es accesible para ambos. Un supermercado de 800-1.500 m² puede instrumentar entradas y zonas críticas con una inversión de entrada moderada y un ROI medible en menos de 12 meses (variable según punto de partida).

### ¿Cómo se integra con el TPV y los sistemas de gestión existentes?

Flame Analytics expone API y conectores para integrar datos de tráfico con TPV, ERP y plataformas de BI. La integración se decide caso a caso según los sistemas del cliente.

### ¿Qué diferencia hay entre conteo de personas y analítica avanzada?

El conteo de personas mide cuántos entran. La analítica avanzada explica qué hacen dentro: por dónde se mueven, dónde se detienen, qué zonas convierten y cuáles no. Una decisión informada necesita las dos capas.

### ¿Se puede comparar el rendimiento de tiendas con tamaños y ubicaciones diferentes?

Sí. El benchmarking efectivo usa métricas relativas — tasa de conversión, tiempo de permanencia por zona, ventas por m² — que normalizan las diferencias de tamaño y contexto. La clave es segmentar la red en grupos de tiendas comparables y analizar tendencias, no cifras absolutas.

### ¿Cuántas tiendas necesito para que la analítica de red tenga sentido?

No hay un mínimo técnico. Desde dos tiendas, la comparación ya genera valor — detectar diferencias de conversión o comportamiento entre dos ubicaciones permite tomar decisiones más informadas. El valor del benchmarking crece con cada tienda que se añade a la red, porque los patrones se hacen más claros y las buenas prácticas más evidentes.

### ¿Es necesario cambiar las cámaras existentes para implementar analítica de red?

No. El Hypersensor de Flame se instala sobre la infraestructura de cámaras existente. No requiere obra ni sustitución de equipos — es una capa de inteligencia que se añade sobre lo que cada tienda ya tiene.

### ¿La plataforma cumple con el RGPD en todos los países?

Sí. La gestión de tiendas con Flame opera sin biometría y sin almacenamiento de vídeo bruto. Los datos son siempre agregados y anonimizados. Este enfoque de privacidad por diseño cumple con el RGPD y con las normativas de protección de datos de los principales mercados internacionales. Más detalles en nuestra guía de cumplimiento RGPD.

### ¿Cómo se accede a los datos de toda la red?

A través de un dashboard centralizado accesible desde cualquier navegador. El director de operaciones ve la red completa en una vista, con la posibilidad de filtrar por tienda, zona geográfica, periodo o tipo de métrica. También es posible configurar alertas automáticas y reporting periódico por email.

### ¿Qué es la inteligencia artificial retail aplicada a analítica?

La inteligencia artificial retail es la aplicación de machine learning y visión artificial a los datos comportamentales generados dentro de tiendas físicas. Cubre conteo de personas, heatmaps de movimiento, medición de tiempo de permanencia, detección de colas, predicción de afluencia y atribución de campañas — todo sin identificar a clientes individuales.

### ¿Es diferente de la analítica ecommerce?

Sí. La analítica ecommerce rastrea sesiones individuales y transacciones. La analítica de tienda física con IA trabaja a nivel agregado — mide flujos, patrones y ocupación sobre una población, no clickstreams individuales. Esto la hace privacidad-compliant por diseño, pero también significa que las decisiones que informa son principalmente operativas y espaciales.

### ¿Hay que cambiar las cámaras existentes?

En la mayoría de casos, no. Las plataformas modernas de video analítica con IA están diseñadas para añadir inteligencia sobre la infraestructura CCTV existente. El modelo de IA se ejecuta en un dispositivo edge que se conecta a los feeds de cámaras existentes, eliminando la necesidad de sustituir hardware.

### ¿Es compatible con el RGPD?

Puede serlo, y las mejores plataformas están diseñadas específicamente para cumplir el RGPD. Los criterios clave son: sin reconocimiento facial, sin procesamiento biométrico, sin seguimiento individual y sin retención de vídeo bruto. Cuando se cumplen estas condiciones — como en la arquitectura de Flame — no hay procesamiento de datos personales. Consulta nuestra guía RGPD para video analítica retail.

### ¿Qué tipos de retailers se benefician más?

Cualquier formato de retail físico donde la afluencia, el layout, el coste de personal o la efectividad promocional sean variables de negocio relevantes. En la práctica: moda, alimentación, deporte, electrónica, hogar y centros comerciales. El caso de ROI es más fuerte para operadores multisede, donde una infraestructura de datos consistente desbloquea insights a nivel de portfolio.

### Descubre cómo Flame Analytics mide la inteligencia de tu tienda

Conteo de personas, heatmaps, predicción de afluencia y video analítica con inteligencia artificial retail compatible con RGPD. Sin biometría. Sin caja negra. Solicita una demo

### ¿Cuál es el tipo de campaña más efectivo para centros comerciales?

Las campañas de eventos estacionales generan el mayor incremento bruto de afluencia (18-35%), pero la publicidad móvil geolocalizada ofrece el mejor coste por visita incremental para activación continua. La estrategia más efectiva combina ambas: eventos para períodos pico y geotargeting continuo para períodos valle.

### ¿Cómo se mide el ROI de una campaña en un centro comercial?

La medición requiere tres datos: inversión en campaña, incremento de afluencia contra la línea base, e ingreso medio por visitante. La afluencia incremental se calcula comparando el tráfico observado durante la campaña contra la previsión para el mismo período sin campaña.

### ¿Se pueden compartir los datos de afluencia con los operadores?

Sí, y es uno de los usos de mayor valor. Los operadores reciben datos agregados de afluencia por zona mostrando el tráfico antes, durante y después de las campañas. Esto refuerza la relación con los inquilinos y crea base para coinversión. No hay seguimiento individual ni datos personales.

### ¿Qué tecnología de analítica usan los centros comerciales más avanzados?

Combinan contadores de entrada, sensores WiFi/Bluetooth y plataformas de video analítica con IA. La video analítica con IA — ejecutándose en dispositivos edge — proporciona los datos más granulares: heatmaps por zona, tiempo de permanencia, recorrido del cliente y detección de colas. Los criterios clave al evaluarlas son precisión (+95%), arquitectura RGPD e integración con herramientas de BI existentes.

### ¿Cuánto incremento de afluencia puede generar una buena campaña?

Según benchmarks de ICSC y CBRE, las campañas omnicanal bien ejecutadas generan un 20-35% de incremento durante las ventanas de campaña. Las campañas geolocalizadas sin activación in-mall generan típicamente un 10-20%. Estas cifras asumen un marco de medición con línea base establecida.

### ¿La video-analítica necesita consentimiento del visitante?

Depende del tipo de datos. Si el sistema produce exclusivamente datos agregados y anónimos (conteos, heatmaps, flujos) sin posibilidad de identificar a individuos, no se trata de datos personales y por tanto no necesitas consentimiento ni ninguna base legal del RGPD. 9.

### ¿Puedo usar mis cámaras CCTV para analítica sin cambiar nada?

Técnicamente sí, si utilizas un sistema como Hypersensor que se conecta al flujo de vídeo existente. Legalmente, debes actualizar tu cartelería y registro de actividades para reflejar la nueva finalidad (analítica además de seguridad). Si el sistema no usa biometría, los requisitos adicionales son mínimos.

### ¿Qué dice el EU AI Act sobre video-analítica en centros comerciales?

El EU AI Act clasifica los sistemas de identificación biométrica remota en espacios públicos como de alto riesgo o prohibidos. Sin embargo, los sistemas de analítica que no realizan identificación biométrica — como el conteo de personas o la generación de mapas de calor mediante detección de siluetas — no entran en esta clasificación restrictiva.

### ¿Es legal medir el tiempo de permanencia de los visitantes?

Sí, siempre que la medición sea anónima y agregada. Un sistema que mide “tiempo medio de permanencia en zona A: 4,2 minutos” con datos estadísticos no trata datos personales. Un sistema que registra “el visitante con ID #X47 permaneció 4,2 minutos” genera un dato potencialmente personal dependiendo de si ese ID puede vincularse a una persona.

### ¿Qué multas se han impuesto por video-analítica no conforme?

En todos los casos, el denominador común fue el uso de biometría sin base legal adecuada.

### ¿Cuánto cuesta un sistema de cuenta personas?

Depende de la tecnología. Un sensor infrarrojo básico cuesta 100-300 euros. Un sensor estereoscópico dedicado, 500-2.000 euros por punto. Un sistema basado en IA sobre CCTV existente como Flame elimina el coste de hardware — solo pagas la licencia de software.

### ¿Qué precisión tiene el cuenta personas con IA?

Superior al 95% en condiciones normales. Los algoritmos incluyen exclusión automática de personal, detección de grupos y corrección de doble conteo con cámaras superpuestas.

### ¿El cuenta personas cumple con el RGPD?

Depende del sistema. Flame Hypersensor opera exclusivamente con detección de siluetas y datos agregados anónimos — cumplimiento total con RGPD y EU AI Act.

### ¿Puedo usar mis cámaras de seguridad actuales?

Sí, si son cámaras IP con protocolo RTSP u ONVIF. Esto incluye prácticamente todas las cámaras instaladas en los últimos 10 años: Hikvision, Dahua, Axis, Bosch, Hanwha y cualquier modelo compatible.

### ¿Cuánto tarda la implementación?

Con un sistema basado en IA sobre CCTV: 5-10 días laborables para una tienda, 4-6 semanas para una red de centros comerciales. Con sensores dedicados el plazo se duplica por la instalación física.

### ¿Se puede integrar con mi TPV?

Sí. Los sistemas de cuenta personas más completos, como Flame, ofrecen integraciones nativas con los principales TPV del mercado (Oracle Retail, SAP, Shopify POS, entre otros) y también mediante API abierta. La integración con el TPV es lo que permite calcular automáticamente la tasa de conversión real (transacciones / visitantes) sin intervención manual. Los datos de tráfico se cruzan con los tickets de venta en tiempo real, de forma que en el dashboard puedes ver la conversión actualizada hora a hora.

### ¿Qué pasa con la iluminación o contraluces?

Las condiciones de iluminación son uno de los retos clásicos del cuenta personas basado en vídeo. Los contraluces fuertes (por ejemplo, una entrada con cristaleras orientadas al sur) pueden dificultar la detección si la cámara no tiene rango dinámico amplio (WDR). Los algoritmos de IA modernos mitigan este problema mediante técnicas de normalización de imagen y modelos entrenados con miles de escenarios de iluminación adversa. Aun así, durante la fase de auditoría es importante evaluar los puntos con peor iluminación y, si es necesario, ajustar la posición o los parámetros de exposición de la cámara. En la práctica, con cámaras IP de gama media instaladas en los últimos 5 años, los problemas de iluminación rara vez afectan a la precisión por debajo del 93%.

### ¿Necesito cambiar mis cámaras de seguridad actuales?

En la mayoría de casos, no. Hypersensor es compatible con cualquier cámara IP que soporte RTSP u ONVIF, lo que incluye prácticamente todas las cámaras instaladas en los últimos 10 años (Hikvision, Dahua, Axis, Bosch, Hanwha, etc.).

### ¿La analítica de vídeo cumple con el RGPD?

Depende del sistema. Hypersensor opera exclusivamente con detección de siluetas y datos agregados anónimos, sin recopilar ningún dato personal. Cumplimiento total con RGPD y EU AI Act.

### ¿Qué precisión tiene el conteo?

Superior al 95% en condiciones normales de operación. El sistema incluye exclusión automática de personal, detección de grupos y corrección de doble conteo en entornos con múltiples cámaras superpuestas.

### ¿El vídeo se envía a la nube?

No. Todo el procesamiento se ejecuta en el edge (servidor local en el establecimiento). Solo los datos estructurados (números, métricas, alertas) se envían al dashboard en la nube. El vídeo nunca sale de la tienda.

### ¿Qué diferencia hay entre visitas y visitantes únicos?

Una visita es cada entrada al centro; un visitante único es cada persona distinta en un periodo. Si un mismo cliente entra dos veces en el mes, cuenta como 2 visitas y 1 visitante único. Dividir visitas entre visitantes únicos da la frecuencia de visita, que en un centro comercial español sano se mueve entre 1,8 y 2,4 visitas al mes por visitante.

### ¿Se puede medir la conversión en una tienda física como en un ecommerce?

Sí. Combinando el conteo de personas con los datos del TPV se obtiene el mismo embudo que mide una tienda online: cuántos entran, cuántos compran y cuánto gastan. La ecuación Venta = Tráfico × Conversión × Ticket medio funciona igual en ambos canales, y optimizarla en el espacio físico es el equivalente al CRO del comercio electrónico.

### ¿Cómo se mide la fidelidad de los visitantes sin un programa de puntos?

Con analítica de presencia por wifi, que detecta de forma anónima y agregada cuándo un dispositivo vuelve al centro. Así se calculan la tasa de retorno, el ratio de repetición y la frecuencia de visita sin pedir ningún registro al visitante. Un descenso sostenido de la repetición es la señal más temprana de pérdida de clientela base.

### ¿Por dónde empiezo si mi centro no mide casi nada?

Por el conteo de personas en los accesos principales: es el dato raíz sobre el que se calcula todo lo demás. A partir de ahí, el plan de 60 días descrito en esta guía añade la medición por zonas, la integración de datos demográficos y el dashboard compartido con dirección y operadores. Lo importante es definir antes qué decisiones cambiarán con cada dato.

### ¿Con qué frecuencia hay que revisar estos KPIs?

El cuadro de mando operativo se revisa cada semana con dirección y comité de operadores; las tendencias estructurales (captación del área de influencia, ratio de repetición, demografía) se evalúan en comparativa interanual, siempre entre periodos equivalentes. Una caída interanual sostenida durante seis meses es el umbral que separa el ruido de un problema real.

### ¿Es legal hacer wifi marketing con el RGPD?

Sí, siempre que los datos se capten con consentimiento expreso. El portal cautivo debe informar de quién trata los datos y con qué finalidad, enlazar la política de privacidad y permitir ejercer los derechos de acceso, rectificación y supresión. El usuario decide libremente si se registra a cambio de la conexión.

### ¿El wifi marketing detecta todos los móviles que pasan por delante?

No. El guest wifi actual trabaja únicamente con los usuarios que se conectan de forma voluntaria a través del portal de acceso. La detección pasiva de dispositivos por dirección MAC dejó de ser fiable (los móviles modernos usan direcciones aleatorias) y no encaja con el RGPD, así que la base del wifi marketing es el registro consentido.

### ¿Qué datos conviene pedir en el portal de acceso?

Los mínimos imprescindibles para tu estrategia: normalmente nombre y correo electrónico, y de forma opcional la fecha de nacimiento si quieres lanzar campañas de cumpleaños. Cuanta menos fricción tenga el registro, más usuarios completarán el acceso y más rápido crecerá tu base de datos.

### ¿El guest wifi sirve solo para grandes superficies?

No. La misma lógica funciona en cualquier espacio con visitas físicas: centros comerciales, cadenas de retail, hoteles o restaurantes. Lo que cambia es la prioridad: un centro comercial busca afluencia y fidelidad, un hotel cuida su reputación y el consumo interno, y un restaurante persigue reseñas y repetición.

### ¿Cómo se mide el retorno del wifi marketing?

Con tres indicadores: el crecimiento de la base de datos de clientes registrados, el rendimiento de las campañas (aperturas, clics y canjes de ofertas) y la evolución de la recurrencia de visita. Si las visitas recurrentes y los canjes crecen tras activar el canal, el wifi está generando negocio.

### ¿Van a desaparecer los centros comerciales?

No, pero los que no evolucionen sí. El estudio de Deloitte cifra en un 43 % los centros comerciales españoles que necesitan reposicionamiento, y el profesor Leonard Schlesinger explica el porqué: fueron construidos para patrones de socialización que ya no existen. El futuro pasa por transformarse en espacios de experiencia, ocio y servicios apoyados en datos, no por desaparecer.

### ¿Qué tecnologías definirán el centro comercial del futuro?

Los estudios coinciden en varias capas: analítica de afluencia y ocupación como base de gestión, inteligencia artificial para personalizar y predecir la demanda (Lubelczyk y Brown hablan de pasillos con IA y probadores inteligentes) y experiencias inmersivas con realidad virtual y aumentada, que Ericsson ConsumerLab sitúa como expectativa del consumidor para 2030. La condición transversal es cumplir el RGPD en todo tratamiento de datos de visitantes.

### ¿Qué papel juega la sostenibilidad en los centros comerciales?

Ha pasado de tendencia a requisito. Los expertos consultados por Flame la sitúan entre las prioridades del sector desde 2019: consumo de proximidad, trazabilidad, materiales sostenibles y un rol activo del retail como agente de cambio. Para el gestor es, además, un criterio creciente de los operadores al elegir en qué centros estar.

### ¿Qué es un centro comercial de uso mixto?

Un espacio que combina comercio con restauración, ocio, servicios e incluso otros usos, y que funciona como destino en sí mismo. Responde a lo que detecta el estudio «How We Shop» de Westfield: el consumidor demanda espacios de oferta diversificada donde no solo se va a comprar, sino a vivir experiencias que le conecten con las marcas.

### ¿Por dónde empiezo la transformación de mi centro comercial?

Por la medición. Antes de decidir reformas u operadores hay que conocer la afluencia real del centro: cuántas personas entran, cómo circulan entre zonas, cuánto permanecen y con qué frecuencia repiten. El conteo de personas, la analítica de tráfico y la gestión de ocupación son el primer escalón, y los 10 KPIs esenciales del centro comercial, el cuadro de mando.

### ¿Qué es el marketing de fidelización?

Es el conjunto de estrategias y acciones orientadas a que un cliente que ya ha comprado vuelva a hacerlo, aumente su frecuencia de compra y recomiende la marca. Combina experiencia de cliente, comunicación personalizada, programas de valor añadido y medición continua de la recurrencia.

### ¿Por qué es más rentable retener clientes que captarlos?

Porque captar exige repetir constantemente la inversión en publicidad y promociones, mientras que retener aprovecha una relación que ya existe: el cliente fiel vuelve por iniciativa propia, compra con más confianza y actúa como prescriptor, generando nuevos clientes sin coste publicitario adicional.

### ¿Cómo se mide la fidelidad de un cliente en una tienda física?

Con cuatro métricas principales: la tasa de retorno (porcentaje de visitantes que repiten), la proporción de clientes nuevos frente a recurrentes, la frecuencia de visita y el tiempo de permanencia en tienda. Plataformas de analítica como Flame las obtienen de forma automática y continua a partir del comportamiento real de los visitantes.

### ¿Qué papel juega el wifi de invitados en la fidelización?

Es la puerta de entrada al dato: cuando el cliente se conecta a la red wifi de la tienda, el negocio obtiene un perfil y un histórico de visitas. Con esa información puede segmentar campañas, personalizar ofertas, detectar clientes inactivos y reactivarlos automáticamente, además de medir la recurrencia real de su base de clientes.

### ¿Sirven estos consejos para un centro comercial?

Sí. Los principios son los mismos (experiencia, comunicación, segmentación y medición), aplicados a escala de recinto: el centro comercial mide la recurrencia y la permanencia de sus visitantes, usa el wifi como canal de marketing para todo el complejo y comparte los datos con sus operadores para mejorar la experiencia conjunta.

### ¿Qué es una estrategia omnicanal en retail?

Es la integración de todos los canales de venta y contacto (tienda física, ecommerce, app, redes sociales, atención al cliente) para que el cliente viva una experiencia única y coherente, compre donde compre. No consiste en estar en muchos canales, sino en que todos compartan datos, catálogo y visión del cliente.

### ¿El ecommerce va a acabar con la tienda física?

No. Son canales complementarios con papeles distintos: el online aporta precio, surtido y comodidad; la tienda aporta confianza, asesoramiento, inmediatez y experiencia de marca. Los retailers que mejor funcionan integran ambos mundos en lugar de enfrentarlos.

### ¿Qué es el showrooming y cómo afecta a mi tienda?

Consiste en probar o consultar un producto en la tienda física y comprarlo después online. Para un retailer omnicanal no es una fuga, sino una venta que sigue otro camino. La clave está en medir el valor real de la visita a tienda y en facilitar que la compra se cierre en el canal propio, sea cual sea.

### ¿Cómo puedo medir la conversión de mi tienda física?

Necesitas dos datos: cuántas personas entran (con un sistema de conteo) y cuántos tickets registra tu caja. Dividiendo tickets entre visitas obtienes la tasa de conversión de la tienda, el equivalente directo a la del ecommerce. En nuestra guía completa del cuenta personas para retail explicamos cómo hacerlo paso a paso.

### ¿Por dónde empiezo con la analítica in-store?

Lo habitual es empezar por el conteo de personas, que te da visitas y tasa de conversión, y ampliar después con mapas de calor, permanencia y recorridos. Si quieres ver cómo funcionaría en tu negocio, contacta con nuestro equipo y te lo mostramos con tus datos.

### ¿Qué es un sistema de conteo de personas?

Un sistema de conteo de personas mide automáticamente cuántas personas entran y salen de un espacio físico, distinguiendo entradas de salidas, excluyendo empleados y entregando datos en tiempo real. Las plataformas modernas amplían el conteo con métricas de comportamiento (recorridos, zonas calientes), conversión y ocupación.

### ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre las plataformas de 2ª y 3ª generación?

Las plataformas de 2ª generación (FootfallCam, V-Count, RetailNext) requieren la instalación de sensores propios (estereoscópicos, térmicos o IoT) en cada punto de medición. Las plataformas de 3ª generación (como Flame Analytics) ejecutan la analítica de IA directamente sobre las cámaras CCTV existentes, eliminando el hardware nuevo.

### ¿Es ShopperTrak una empresa independiente?

No desde 2016. ShopperTrak fue adquirida por Tyco por 175 millones de dólares en enero de 2016 y, desde 2019, opera como una de las líneas de producto de Sensormatic Solutions, marca paraguas de Johnson Controls.

### ¿Todas las plataformas cumplen RGPD?

Las cinco plataformas analizadas declaran cumplimiento RGPD. Las diferencias relevantes están en (a) si los datos se almacenan en la UE o fuera, y (b) si la arquitectura técnica usa biometría o solo detección anónima por silueta. Para sectores con requisitos estrictos (banca, salud, contratos públicos), conviene confirmar ambas cuestiones por escrito antes de contratar.

### ¿Puedo usar mis cámaras de seguridad actuales para conteo de personas?

Solo con las plataformas de 3ª generación (IA on-CCTV) como Flame Analytics. Las plataformas basadas en sensores propios (FootfallCam, V-Count, RetailNext, ShopperTrak en su línea principal) requieren instalar su hardware específico en cada local, aunque algunas ofrezcan también analítica complementaria sobre cámaras IP.

### ¿Cuál es el coste típico de implementación?

Un sensor estereoscópico dedicado cuesta entre 500 y 2.000 € por punto de medición, más la licencia de software. Las plataformas IA on-CCTV eliminan el coste de hardware si las cámaras existentes cumplen los requisitos mínimos (típicamente 720p y posición cenital o angular). En todos los casos, el coste de licencia anual depende del número de puntos y módulos contratados.

### ¿Cuánto tarda en estar operativo un sistema de conteo de personas?

Varía según el modelo. Una plataforma IA on-CCTV puede entregar datos en 5-7 días por punto si la red de cámaras existente es compatible. Un despliegue con sensores dedicados (instalación física + cableado + calibración) puede requerir entre 4 y 12 semanas, especialmente en redes multi-tienda.

### ¿Cuál es el mejor sistema de conteo de personas en 2026?

No existe un «mejor» universal: depende de tu infraestructura y prioridades. Si ya tienes CCTV, una plataforma de 3ª generación como Flame Analytics evita comprar hardware nuevo y se despliega en días. Si no tienes cámaras y prefieres un único proveedor de hardware + software, FootfallCam o V-Count son candidatos sólidos. Para enterprise norteamericano con equipos de BI, RetailNext y ShopperTrak (Sensormatic) son los habituales.

### ¿Por qué Xovis y Axis no están en la comparativa principal?

Ambos son fabricantes relevantes, pero su propuesta es principalmente sensórica: Xovis fabrica sensores 3D propios (líder en aeropuertos) y AXIS People Counter es una aplicación embebida que corre solo en cámaras Axis. Las cinco plataformas comparadas ofrecen, además del conteo, una capa completa de analítica de negocio para retail: conversión, permanencia, recorridos y comparativas entre tiendas.

### Is people counting with video cameras GDPR-compliant?

Yes, when done correctly. People counting that produces only aggregate numbers (e.g., “142 visitors entered between 14:00 and 15:00”) without identifying or tracking individuals is compatible with GDPR. The key is that the system processes video frames to extract counts and immediately discards the imagery, never generating personal data as output. A DPIA is still recommended given the use of cameras in public spaces.

### Do I need consent to use video analytics in a shopping mall?

Not necessarily. Most video analytics in retail rely on “legitimate interest” (Art. 6.1f) rather than consent, since obtaining explicit consent from every visitor entering a mall is impractical. However, you must conduct a legitimate interest assessment (LIA), ensure proper signage, and demonstrate that the processing does not override visitors’ rights and freedoms. If your system processes biometric data (Art. 9), legitimate interest alone is insufficient — explicit consent or another Art. 9 exemption is required.

### What is the difference between GDPR and the EU AI Act for video analytics?

The GDPR regulates the processing of personal data regardless of the technology used. The EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) specifically regulates AI systems by risk level. Real-time biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces is banned outright under the AI Act. AI-based video analytics that do not involve biometric identification may still be classified as “high-risk” under Annex III, requiring conformity assessments, transparency obligations, and human oversight. Both regulations apply simultaneously — compliance with one does not guarantee compliance with the other.

### Can I use heatmaps in my shopping mall without violating GDPR?

Yes. Heatmaps that show aggregate foot traffic patterns across zones — without tracking or identifying specific individuals — are fully compatible with GDPR. The technology counts the density of people in defined areas over time and produces a visual overlay. As long as the underlying system does not generate individual trajectories linked to biometric or personal identifiers, heatmaps represent anonymised statistical output. Flame’s Hypersensor generates heatmaps using exactly this approach.

### How long can I store video analytics data under GDPR?

It depends on what type of data. Raw CCTV footage containing identifiable individuals should typically be retained for no more than 72 hours (per most EU DPA guidance), unless a specific security incident justifies longer retention. Anonymised analytics data — aggregate counts, heatmaps, dwell time averages — is not personal data and therefore falls outside GDPR retention limits entirely. You can store anonymised analytics data indefinitely for trend analysis and benchmarking.

### How much does a people counting system cost?

Depende de la tecnología. Un sensor infrarrojo básico cuesta 100-300€. Un sensor estereoscópico dedicado, 500-2.000€ por punto. Un sistema basado en AI on existing CCTV como Flame elimina el coste de hardware — solo pagas la licencia de software.

### How accurate is AI-based people counting?

Over 95% under normal conditions. Algorithms include automatic staff exclusion, group detection, and double-counting correction with overlapping cameras.

### Does people counting comply with GDPR?

It depends on the system. Flame Hypersensor operates exclusively with silhouette detection and anonymous aggregated data — full GDPR and EU AI Act compliance.

### Can I use my current security cameras?

Yes, if they are IP cameras with RTSP or ONVIF protocol. This includes virtually all cameras installed in the last 10 years: Hikvision, Dahua, Axis, Bosch, Hanwha, and any compatible model.

### How long does implementation take?

With an AI-based CCTV system: 5-10 business days for a store, 4-6 weeks for a shopping mall network. With dedicated sensors, the timeline doubles due to physical installation.

### Do I need to replace my current security cameras?

In most cases, no. Hypersensor is compatible with any IP camera that supports RTSP or ONVIF, which includes virtually all cameras installed in the last 10 years (Hikvision, Dahua, Axis, Bosch, Hanwha, etc.).

### Does video analytics comply with GDPR?

It depends on the system. Hypersensor operates exclusively with silhouette detection and anonymous aggregated data, without collecting any personal data. Full GDPR and EU AI Act compliance.

### How accurate is the counting?

Over 95% under normal operating conditions. The system includes automatic staff exclusion, group detection, and double-counting correction in environments with overlapping cameras.

### Is the video sent to the cloud?

No. All processing runs at the edge (local server at the premises). Only structured data (numbers, metrics, alerts) is sent to the cloud dashboard. Video never leaves the store.

### What is people counting software?

People counting software automatically measures how many people enter and leave a physical space, distinguishing entries from exits, excluding staff and delivering real-time data. Modern platforms extend counting with behavior metrics (journeys, hot zones), conversion rate and occupancy.

### What is the best people counting system for retail?

There is no universal best: it depends on your infrastructure and priorities. If you already have CCTV, a 3rd-generation AI-on-CCTV platform like Flame Analytics avoids buying hardware and deploys in days. If you have no cameras and want a single hardware + software vendor, FootfallCam or V-Count are solid candidates. For North American enterprise chains with BI teams, RetailNext and ShopperTrak (Sensormatic) are the usual picks.

### Can I use my existing security cameras for people counting?

Only with 3rd-generation (AI-on-CCTV) platforms such as Flame Analytics. Sensor-based platforms (FootfallCam, V-Count, RetailNext, ShopperTrak in its main line) require installing their specific hardware in every store, although some also offer complementary analytics on IP cameras.

### How accurate are people counting systems?

It depends on the technology generation: infrared beam counters typically reach 70-85% accuracy, 2nd-generation stereo and thermal sensors 85-95%, and 3rd-generation AI computer vision on CCTV 95-98% or higher, provided the cameras meet minimum requirements.

### Are people counting systems GDPR compliant?

All five platforms analyzed declare GDPR compliance. The relevant differences are (a) whether data is stored in the EU or outside, and (b) whether the technical architecture uses biometrics or only anonymous silhouette detection. For sectors with strict requirements (banking, healthcare, public contracts), confirm both points in writing before signing.

### How long does it take to deploy a people counting system?

It varies by model. An AI-on-CCTV platform can deliver data within 5-7 days per site if the existing camera network is compatible. A rollout with dedicated sensors (physical installation, cabling, calibration) can take between 4 and 12 weeks, especially across multi-store networks.
